clue.text: Cat gets a bit of rabbit stuck in the throat

indicators.note: something stuck in another sits inside it, so these pieces go inside the cat

parts.note: the lynx is a wild cat

indicators.note: a bit of the word rabbit is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A cat chokes on a mouthful of rabbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck in' puts A and R (the first letter of rabbit) inside LYNX.
explanation.definitionFit: The voice box sits in the throat, so the anatomical name stands loosely for that part of the neck.

clue.text: Support suspension of delivery

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair
a break is a pause or suspension of activity

explanation.surface: A halt in deliveries of supporting equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: A leg break is a cricket ball spun by the bowler from leg side to off side; in cricket a bowled ball is a delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a leg break is a type of ball bowled, and each bowled ball is called a delivery.

clue.text: Quack remedy Ada got off the shelf

indicators.note: a quack remedy is fake, so the words remedy Ada are made into something counterfeit

explanation.surface: Ada bought a dubious cure straight off the shop shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready-made goods are bought finished, not made to order, just as off-the-shelf ones are.

clue.text: Son caught in trap? Retreat!

indicators.note: the son ends up inside the trap

parts.note: a net is used to trap fish or animals
S is the abbreviation for son in family trees

explanation.surface: A warning shout as a boy is caught in a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest is a cosy refuge or hideaway, a place of retreat.

clue.text: Drills type of junction box

parts.note: to drill pupils is to teach them by repetition
a T-junction is where one road meets another at right angles

explanation.surface: A puzzle-like listing of drills and junction boxes from a hardware catalogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea chest is a large wooden box once used to ship tea, now for moving house.

clue.text: Exterminate troublesome mice constantly present in the locality

parts.note: to end something is to finish it off or wipe it out

indicators.note: troublesome mice are unruly, so the word mice is jumbled

explanation.surface: Wiping out a pest problem of mice that keeps recurring locally.
explanation.definitionFit: An endemic disease or species is native to and regularly found in a particular area.

clue.text: Profitable advertisement

definitions.meaning: making money, as a ... venture does

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for money-making and a noun for a broadcast advert.

clue.text: King Edward contracted fungal disease

parts.note: ER stands for Edwardus Rex, King Edward
to contract an illness is to get it, past tense got

explanation.surface: A monarch caught a crop blight.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is also a British potato variety, adding to the farming picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergot is a fungus that infects rye and other cereals, causing disease.

clue.text: Gods making birds fly round a pole

indicators.note: the birds go round the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: tits are small songbirds
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: Birds circling a pole create something godlike.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Titans were the elder generation of deities overthrown by Zeus.

clue.text: Prepared veg that is found in old club

parts.note: mash is mashed potato
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Mashed potato discovered in an old golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A mashie was an old-fashioned iron golf club, roughly a modern five iron.

clue.text: Beast left in splendid pasture

indicators.note: the beast and left go inside the word for splendid

parts.note: grand means splendid or magnificent
an ass is a beast of burden

explanation.surface: A donkey turned out into a fine meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: Grassland is open land covered in grass, used as pasture for grazing animals.

clue.text: Could show strength

definitions.meaning: power or force, as in 'with all his ...'

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a modal verb of possibility and a noun for physical power.

clue.text: Reportedly breed fish

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word for breed is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to raise animals is to breed them

explanation.surface: A rumour about breeding fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Rays are flat cartilaginous fish such as skates and stingrays.

clue.text: Legislative body has money for wine

parts.note: a parliamentary house is called a chamber
tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: A parliament spends its funds on wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambertin is a celebrated red Burgundy from Gevrey-Chambertin.

clue.text: Passed away consuming liquor when low

indicators.note: the word for passed away swallows the drink, holding it inside

parts.note: died means passed away
spirit is distilled liquor

explanation.surface: Someone who died after drinking while depressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispirited means low in spirits, downcast.

clue.text: Greed is a sin consuming a resistance leader

indicators.note: the sin eats up the following pieces, which go inside it

parts.note: a vice is a moral failing or sin

indicators.note: the leader of the word resistance is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A moral lesson: greed is a sin that devours the leader of the resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consuming' puts A and R inside VICE, after the first A.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is an extreme desire for wealth, a close synonym of greed.

clue.text: Bird starts to like eating shellfish

parts.note: a cock is a male bird, especially a rooster

indicators.note: the starts of the words like and eating give their first letters

explanation.surface: A bird that has started to enjoy eating shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockle is a small edible bivalve mollusc.

clue.text: Become despondent as the role gets changed

indicators.note: the words as the role are altered into a different order

explanation.surface: An actor loses heart as a role is rewritten.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose heart is to lose courage and hope, becoming downcast.

clue.text: Maps feature National Trust island — land that was lost

indicators.note: the atlas has these pieces as its feature, set within it

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps
NT is the abbreviation for the National Trust, the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: Maps show a heritage-listed island, a lost land.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlantis is the legendary island said by Plato to have sunk beneath the sea.

clue.text: Posted letters for autocrat

indicators.note: the letters of the word posted are the material, rearranged to make a new word

explanation.surface: A tyrant receives letters in the post.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is a ruler with absolute power, another word for an autocrat.

clue.text: A number embrace goddess? That's capital!

indicators.note: the number wraps its arms round the goddess

parts.note: ten is a number
Hera is the Greek queen of the gods

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims with delight on embracing a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's capital!' sounds like an old exclamation of delight, but 'capital' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Teheran, or Tehran, is the capital city of Iran.

clue.text: Apathetic group becomes determined

parts.note: dead can mean lifeless or unresponsive, as an apathetic crowd is
a set is a group of things or people

explanation.surface: A listless band suddenly finds resolve.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dead set on something means being firmly resolved to do it.

clue.text: Judge finds detectives taken in by banker

indicators.note: the detectives are held inside the river

parts.note: a banker in crosswords is a river, something with banks; the Dee is one
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

explanation.surface: A judge discovers detectives have been duped by a financier.
explanation.definitionFit: To decide is to judge or settle a question.

clue.text: Finished one small drink

parts.note: past means over or finished
I is the Roman numeral one
S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Someone has finished a small drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastis is an aniseed-flavoured French aperitif.

clue.text: Dessert wine gives one the shakes later

parts.note: afters is British informal for the pudding course
hock is a German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: Pudding wine leaves a diner trembling afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: AFTERS is everyday British for dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: An aftershock is a smaller tremor following a major earthquake: shaking that comes later.

clue.text: Duplicate bridge player can get into knots

parts.note: a twin is an exact copy
E is East, one of the four players at bridge

explanation.surface: Duplicate bridge, a form of the card game, can tie players up in knots.
explanation.walkthrough: Duplicate bridge is a competitive form of the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: To twine is to twist or wind together, tangling strands as a knot does.

clue.text: Bird featured in banner headline

indicators.note: the bird is a feature within the words banner headline, running across them

explanation.surface: A bird makes the front-page headline.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless South American bird related to the ostrich.

clue.text: Bird's speed

definitions.meaning: a small wading bird of the sandpiper family
a nautical mile per hour, a unit of speed at sea

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a shorebird and a unit of speed used for ships and aircraft.

clue.text: Boy wanting more tobacco

definitions.meaning: Dickens's orphan Oliver famously asks for more gruel
a rope of tobacco leaves wound together

explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Twist is the Dickens boy who asked for more; a twist is also a form of tobacco.

clue.text: Dan turned ugly when laid off

indicators.note: an ugly change leaves the words Dan turned in a disordered new shape

explanation.surface: Dan turned nasty when he was sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'ugly' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers made redundant have lost their jobs because they are no longer needed.

clue.text: Society awaiting settlement of expenses

parts.note: a pending matter is one not yet settled

explanation.surface: A club's expenses claim not yet paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Spending is money laid out, the outgoings or expenses of a person or body.

clue.text: Condition of works of art head of Egyptologists removed

indicators.note: the named letter is taken away from the works of art

parts.note: statues are sculpted works of art

indicators.note: the head of the word Egyptologists is its first letter

explanation.surface: Egyptian statues in poor condition after an archaeologist was removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' takes E (the head of Egyptologists) out of STATUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Status means a state of affairs or standing, as in 'current status'.
